findings.claim: The body still tells the parent to send the reviewer the diff (up to 150 KB), while the new OpenCode line in references/launch.md says to send the brief without the diff. The two instructions conflict, and the engine's frozen-context verb may refuse or misread a brief that already carries a diff (more than one base/head pair, or an over-limit reply). The contract does not say that the OpenCode rule overrides the body line.

The Codex launch rule (pipe the brief to `review launch`, never a native reviewer sub-agent) is no longer in the always-read body. It now sits behind a pointer, so a Codex foreman that does not open references/launch.md can launch a native reviewer sub-agent. Other runtimes' contract text changed in the same edit, and the commit itself says role-chain needs the owner's re-approval.

attachFrozenContext mutates input.prompt in place. If the hook runs a second time on the same call object (a retry or re-dispatch), the already-expanded prompt contains the brief and a frozen-context block. The verb would then likely refuse it as more than one base/head pair, or the prompt would be duplicated, and a launch that was valid the first time would be denied. The code has no idempotence guard.

evidence: Reviewed the full diff only; no tools or worktree access were used.
Plugin ordering (gate, then attachFrozenContext, then injectContract) matches the stated design.
The failure paths covered by the tests (refusal, missing engine, timeout, empty reply) deny the launch and leave the prompt unchanged.
